title: From weakly to strongly-interacting driven-dissipative bosons in one dimension
authors: Martina Zündel, Loïc Herviou, Léonie Canet, Anna Minguzzi
abstract: We consider a one-dimensional driven-dissipative Bose-Hubbard model subjected to incoherent pump and one- and two-body losses, and analyze it by studying its two-point space-time correlations. By employing a combination of numerical methods, such as stochastic semi-classical simulations and tensor network methods, as well as perturbation theory within the Keldysh formalism, we characterize the system at varying filling and interaction strength. We present results for two complementary regimes: i) at large filling and weak interactions, where we show that Kardar-Parisi-Zhang scaling is visible in the linewidth of the spectral function and ii) at weak filling and strong interactions, where we analyze what remains of the mean field transition and identify a change of nature of the excitations. Our study covers two important regions of the phase diagram of such a system.
summary: The paper investigates the complex dynamics of bosons in a 1D lattice subject to pumping and dissipation. By employing advanced theoretical tools like the Keldysh formalism and tensor networks, the authors characterize how the system behaves when transitioning from weakly to strongly interacting regimes. The findings reveal universal scaling behaviors (KPZ) in some limits while demonstrating fundamental differences between quantum and classical descriptions.
main_problem: The study characterizes driven-dissipative bosonic systems in one dimension across varying filling and interaction strengths, focusing on the transition between weakly and strongly interacting regimes.
main_result: The system exhibits Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling in the weak interaction/large filling regime, while strong interactions reveal a change of nature in excitations compared to mean-field predictions.
method: A combination of Keldysh formalism for deriving actions, stochastic semi-classical simulations, and tensor network methods are employed to analyze quantum dynamics.
model_or_system: The model is a one-dimensional Bose-Hubbard system subjected to incoherent pumping and various particle losses (one-body and two-body). The evolution is governed by the Lindblad master equation or its semi-classical/Keldysh approximations.
key_observables: Two-point space-time correlations, spectral function linewidth $A(\omega, k)$, and first-order correlation function $g^{(1)}(x, t)$.
important_parameters: Filling (density), interaction strength ($U$), pumping rate ($\gamma_p$), and loss rates ($\gamma_l, \gamma_{2l}$). Key regimes include large filling/weak interaction and weak filling/strong interaction.
main_assumptions: The semi-classical limit is used for some analyses, which neglects certain non-linear quantum field terms. The analysis often focuses on stationary or quasi-stationary correlation regimes.
figures_summary: Figure 14 compares semiclassical and quantum predictions for density distributions ($ho$) and occupation probabilities ($p_N$) across different system sizes and loss mechanisms.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the dynamics by first establishing the theoretical framework (Keldysh formalism, Lindblad equation), then investigating specific regimes (weak vs. strong coupling) using appropriate tools (semi-classical vs. tensor networks), and finally comparing results to highlight deviations from mean-field theory.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium dynamics in bosonic systems, which is central to modern AMO physics research involving driven quantum simulators or optical lattices.

In the right panel, the linewidth of one of the two excitation branches vanishes at k = 0, corresponding to the dissipative Goldstone mode associated with the broken U(1) symmetry in the out-of-equilibrium theory.

The width are obtained by fitting Lorentzian curves for each k-slice.
